comments.note: src/plugins/types.ts introduces PersonaMetadata with an index signature ([key: string]: unknown) to allow arbitrary YAML fields. This is pragmatic for the YAML-driven use case but means TypeScript cannot catch typos in named fields when accessing through the index path. Worth revisiting if downstream builders rely heavily on named fields — a discriminated union or Zod schema could provide better type safety.

runner.ts is entirely synchronous. If a future plugin hook (e.g. onSuiteInit for loading remote data) needs to be async, the runner functions would need to be refactored to async + Promise.all / sequential await. No change needed now, but worth documenting as a known future extension point.

The plan's WP-004.md specifies the runner file as src/plugins/plugin-runner.ts but src/index.ts (WP-001 scaffold) had it commented as plugin-runner.js. The file was created as runner.ts (shorter, more idiomatic). The barrel export in index.ts hides this internal detail from consumers, so there is no API break.

comments.note: tests/plugins/plugin-runner.test.ts covers only the immutable-spread pattern for onBuildContext (e.g. return { ...ctx, step1: 'done' }). No test covers mutation-by-reference (plugin mutates ctx in-place and returns the same reference). Runtime analysis confirms the runner handles this correctly (accumulated = plugin.onBuildContext(...) still picks up the same reference), but an explicit test would close the documentation gap raised in the Developer's handoff notes.

runBuildContext has no runtime guard against a plugin returning undefined (violating the Record<string,unknown> return type). If this happens, accumulated becomes undefined and the next plugin receives undefined as ctx. TypeScript strict mode catches this at compile time, so no change is needed for a strict-TS library — but worth noting for future JS consumers or plugin authors who bypass type-checking.

The runner.ts file name differs from the plan spec (plan.md references src/plugins/plugin-runner.ts; implementation uses src/plugins/runner.ts). The barrel export in src/plugins/index.ts hides this internal detail from all consumers, so there is no API break or documentation issue. Low risk.

[documentation-forward] The onBuildContext hook JSDoc in src/plugins/types.ts says the return value 'must include all original keys'. This is a meaningful API contract (a plugin returning a subset would silently drop keys for all downstream plugins) but it is not enforced by the type system or tested. The Documentation agent should either: (a) strengthen the JSDoc to explicitly warn plugin authors about key-dropping risk, or (b) add a note in the README's plugin authoring guide explaining this invariant.
